newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-QUARTERBACK RYPIEN AGREES TO TERMS WITH THE RAMS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-QUARTERBACK RYPIEN AGREES TO TERMS WITH THE RAMS.

text.p: Mark Rypien agreed to a one-year deal to return to the St. Louis Rams on Monday after leaving the team last year in a bitter contract dispute.

Rypien, the Super Bowl XXVI Most Valuable Player and the 1991 National Football League MVP with the Washington Redskins, was expected to compete for the Rams starting job last year, but was unable to agree to terms with the team.
Rypien sat out until he was signed by the Philadelphia Eagles in October as a backup to Ty Detmer after Rodney Peete suffered a season-ending knee injury.
The 34-year-old Rypien, a two-time Pro Bowler, returns to the Rams with coach Dick Vermeil now in charge of the football operation.
Rypien is 47-31 as a starter in the regular season and 5-2 in seven playoff starts. He has connected for 119 touchdowns, while yielding 86 interceptions.
